subject: BYO temporary retention window request - Acme Labs
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BYO temporary retention window request - Acme Labs

Hi team,

Acme Labs (contact: Alice Park) submitted a formal request to retain a small subset of conversational artifacts for 90 days instead of our default 30-day ephemeral retention. They cite ongoing regulatory QA for a pilot and asked whether we can support a temporary carveout tied to their BYOK (customer-managed keys) setup. Attached is their request PDF and a short evidence scope spreadsheet.

Key facts from the ask:
- Scope: 2 specific product integrations (chat transcripts, model request metadata)
- Duration: temporary 90-day window for those artifacts; automatic revert after 6 months total or on request
- Security: they want the retained blobs encrypted with their KMS key (BYOK alias: acme-byo-key) and audit markings that show key IDs and rotation events
- Risk tolerance: they expect proof-of-preservation (audit logs) for the retained set and an attestation of deletion when window ends

Questions for ops/product/security:
1) Feasible without a major infra change? (Marcus)
2) Can Security confirm required audit log granularity & retention for the retained subset? (Grace)
3) Any gating from Compliance or legal on temporary carveouts we should surface? (Lauren)

I propose a quick 30-min triage call today if possible; otherwise I'll consolidate replies and propose next steps.

Attachments: acme_retention_request.pdf, acme_evidence_scope.xlsx

Thanks,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: security@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO temporary retention window request - Acme Labs

Nikhil — thanks for the summary and attachments. Quick read-through thoughts:

- Audit log granularity: we need per-object creation/deletion events, KMS key id used for encryption, and a tamper-evident event stream for the 90-day window. That means we should capture: request_id, object_id, user_id, key_id, timestamp, operation.
- Evidence/attestation: we can provide a signed audit export (JWT-signed) at the end of the window, but we must explicitly scope which tables/indices are retained longer than platform default.
- BYOK considerations: if Acme's key is external (HSM/KMS outside our control), we need an inbound key policy mapping; rotation events must be logged but we cannot rotate their key. We need to confirm if they will accept a read-only key alias or require active rewrap flow.

Operational constraints: temporary carveouts increase indexing & backup windows. If the retained set is small (they claim ~200k events over 90 days), we can probably do this as an exception with minimal infra impact if we:
1) Create a scoped retention tag on the objects
2) Route retention-tagged writes to a 'carveout' tier with explicit audit exports enabled
3) Enforce deletion via a scheduled job and provide the signed export

Action items I need from product (Marcus):
- Confirm expected throughput / QPS for these two integrations and whether they require real-time replay capability.
- Confirm whether product can support a per-account retention tag & the mechanics of routing to the carveout tier.

I'll also need legal/compliance input on the attestation language; looping Lauren for that.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
Security Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO temporary retention window request - Acme Labs

Thanks — read and noted. A few product constraints to call out:

- We currently support account-level retention config but not per-object temporary carveouts. Adding a per-object tag + routing is doable but likely a 2-3 sprint effort to make it safe (testing + audit export plumbing).
- Short-term alternative: we can implement a "scoped retention buffer" by exporting the subset to an encrypted bucket (BYOK-wrapped) and maintain the audit index in our analytics plane for signoff. This is lower-risk and can be done within 1 sprint if security is comfortable with the export flow.

Questions for the triage:
- Do we need live replay (latency < 200ms) from retained artifacts or is this purely for evidence/QC? If live, export approach won't work.
- Are they expecting any SLA extension for data availability during the 90-day window?

If we go export route, next steps:
1) Nikhil to get confirmation from Acme on live access needs.
2) Security to specify required audit fields and signing format.
3) Product to scope one sprint spike for a safe export + attest pipeline and an internal runbook to revert after expiration.

I'll block time for a quick alignment; if this pattern repeats we should consider making scoped-retention a product feature in Q4.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP Product | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Park <alice.park@acmelabs.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO temporary retention window request - Acme Labs

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- We do not need live replay; this is strictly for QA and regulator evidence. Read-only access exported to our secured bucket (encrypted with our KMS) is fine.
- Estimated volume: ~150k events across two integrations over 90 days. Peak QPS low (<8 r/s).
- Attestation: we need a signed audit export (we can accept SHA256-signed manifest) and a deletion confirmation email after the window ends.

I started the DocuSign approval for the temporary exception (link below). Please let me know if Security needs additional info about our key (acme-byo-key).

DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.com/retention_approval_123

Best,
Alice Park
Head of Platform Risk | Acme Labs

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@acmelabs.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BYO temporary retention window request - Acme Labs

  - Marcus: scope 1-sprint export pipeline spike & runbook (plan by Mon)
  - Lauren: draft attestation language and approval checklist (Mon)

I'll schedule a 30-min triage for Monday 10:00am PT to finalize scope and timeline. If anyone needs to move that, flag now.

Thanks,
Nikhil
